The '''Port of Mongla''' is a link sea port, located at [[Mongla Upazila]], [[Khulna Division]], [[Bangladesh]].It is a sea port of [[Khulna]] city which is located near 
to the north. It is the second largest and second busiest seaport of [[Bangladesh]]. Mongla port lies close to the shore of [[Bay of Bengal]] and Pashur river. Mongla is renowned among the major important ports of the [[Bengal delta]]. Due to the increasing congestion in Bangladesh's largest [[Chittagong Port|port in Chittagong]], many international shipping companies have turned to Mongla as an alternative. Also the influence of continuous demanding from all over the country and neighbouring countries made it busier and economically eye catching day by day.<ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|url=http://www.joc.com/port-news/asian-ports/bangladesh-port-expands-shippers-seek-chittagong-alternative_20170607.html |title=Bangladesh port expands as shippers avoid Chittagong |publisher=Joc.com |date=2012-06-05 |access-date=2017-07-24}}</ref>

Also some political and economical influence in [[Khulna]] region from the government also prevailing the development and demand the port Mongla. [[Padma Bridge]] megaproject is a big example of those influence in [[Khulna]] region. Mongla is also a gateway for tourist ships traveling to the largest [[mangrove forest]] of world, the [[Sunderbans]]. It is also marked as a resource of UNESCO World Heritage Site. The port also hosts the [[Mongla Export Processing Zone]] (Mongla EPZ).

==History==
[[File:Crane WHich Used to Carry container at mongla sea port.jpg|thumb|[[Straddle carrier]] at work in Mongla]]
The port was founded in 1950 to serve the southwestern region of [[East Bengal]]. It was originally known as Chalna Port.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.banglapedia.org/index.php?title=Mongla_Port |title=Mongla Port |website=Banglapedia |access-date=2017-07-24}}</ref>

==Geography==
It was formerly located at Chalna, about {{convert|18|km|mi}} upstream on the [[Pasur River]] but it is now located 48 km south of [[Khulna]] city, as established on 11 December 1954. The Port is surrounded and protected by the [[Sundarbans|Sundarban]] mangrove forest.<ref name="other">[http://www.mpa.gov.bd/port-information/other-information.html Mongla Port Authority - Other Information] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328123745/http://www.mpa.gov.bd/port-information/other-information.html |date=28 March 2012 }}</ref> The port is situated at the confluence of the Pasur River and the Mongla River. It lies about {{convert|100|km|abbr=on}} north of the Bay of Bengal.
.

==Port infrastructure==
The port has 11 jetties and 8 warehouses. It uses 12 swinging moorings in deeper sections in the river. The port is connected by the [[Bangladesh Railway]] to the Khulna Metropolitan Area.

==Ship services==
In 2015–16, 636 ships used Mongla port.<ref name="prothom-alo1">{{cite news |url=http://en.prothom-alo.com/economy/news/132991/Mongla-port-capacity-expanding |title=Mongla port capacity expanding |work=Prothom Alo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814222615/http://en.prothom-alo.com/economy/news/132991/Mongla-port-capacity-expanding |archive-date=2017-08-14 |access-date=2017-07-24}}</ref> Mongla is connected to most major ports in the world, particularly Asian ports. Hundreds of ships use the port each year, most of which come via [[Singapore]], [[Hong Kong]] and [[Colombo]]. Mongla is also connected to most [[inland port]]s in Bangladesh, including the [[Port of Dhaka]] and the [[Port of Narayanganj]].

==Trade==
[[File:Rupsha Bridge 15.jpg|thumb|[[Rupsha Bridge]] connects [[Khulna]] and Mongla]]
The port is open for 24 hours and up to 225 metre long ships can enter into the port for discharging cargo. A constraint free large channel is available for anchorage and loading/unloading facilities on both sides for 33 ships at a time.

==Future expansion==
The government of Bangladesh has launched [[dredging]] and jetty construction projects to expand the capacity of Mongla port.<ref name="prothom-alo1"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dredgingtoday.com/2010/07/04/bangladesh-plan-for-mongla-port-development-project-unveiled/ |title=Bangladesh: Plan for Mongla Port Development Project Unveiled |publisher=Dredging Today |date=2010-07-04 |access-date=2017-07-24}}</ref>
